provenance.note: A least-squares fit of the twelve constants in validation/fit.py FITTED_KEYS against reference cases c4-c6 has been run; every other constant here is hand-set from published literature and is not a fitted value. FITTED IS NOT VALIDATED: the fit moved the cost only from 57.300 to 57.288 and did not reach the reference values. Cases c4 and c5 still model a 150 MW peak against 30 and 20 MW measured, and `solit2 validate` exits non-zero and lists every miss. No constant rests on a bound, but that is flatness and not success: the assumed 90 um spray of the reference nozzle fully evaporates during its 0.9 m fall to the fuel top at any gas temperature rise above roughly 100 K, at every evaporation constant inside the fitted bounds, so almost no water reaches the fuel and the suppression constants have almost no gradient left to fit. evaporation_k_ref_m2s, pool_burning_rate_reduction and pool_extinction_flux_mm_min did not move at all. All three reference cases also rest on an ASSUMED nozzle specification, because SOLIT2 Annex 2 publishes the application density but neither the K-factor nor the droplet spectrum, so these constants have absorbed that assumption and do not transfer to a different nozzle without new test data. `anchor` names the reference cases a constant was set against; it must name only cases that still exist in validation/anchors, or "none".
provenance.reference_cases: SOLIT2 Engineering Guidance Annex 2, full-scale fire tests c4 (Class A with cover), c5 (Class A without cover) and c6 (Class B diesel pools).

pool_ramp_s.note: Annex 2: pools need 2-3 min to develop

pool_extinction_time_s.note: per pool; Annex 2: extinguished pool by pool

critical_velocity_height.note: H in Li-Ingason; mean height gives ~5% lower u_c

flame_length_coefficient.note: C_f, Ingason & Li, Tunnel Fire Dynamics ch.11

ceiling_excess_coefficient.note: scale on the Li & Ingason maximum ceiling excess, absorbing correlation magnitude error and the assumed fire-base height; 1.0 is the unscaled correlation

eta_max.note: SOLIT2 held a 150 MW potential load to ~30 MW, so the ceiling is at least 0.80

w_ref_mm_min.note: basis removed with c1-c3; refit required. Was set against reference cases c1, c2 and c3, none of which survive in validation/anchors, so this value currently rests on nothing and is carried unchanged only to avoid silently altering the physics.

chi_cool_max.note: basis removed with c3; refit required. This value has no surviving reference case and is carried unchanged pending a refit against c4-c6.

evaporation_k_ref_m2s.note: basis removed with c3; refit required. d-squared law constant at the reference gas temperature rise; a 100 um drop evaporates in ~0.1 s at that rise and essentially not at all in cool air. The magnitude is physically reasonable but the specific value was set against c3, which no longer exists.

evaporation_reference_delta_t_k.note: basis removed with c3; refit required. Paired with evaporation_k_ref_m2s and set against the same deleted reference case.

flank_reach_factor.note: lateral band, as a multiple of fuel height, in which descending spray strikes the fuel's sides

flank_efficiency.note: effectiveness of water striking a vertical face relative to water landing on the top face

shielding_reference_loading_kgm3.note: water mass loading at which the droplet's local environment departs materially from the ambient plume; below it a droplet is effectively alone, above it the spray core is partly self-shielded. The starting value and the fitted bounds are an order-of-magnitude engineering guess, NOT a literature figure.

shielding_floor.note: minimum shield factor at very high loading; the spray still entrains hot ambient gas so full insulation from it is not physical. Deliberately NOT fitted: it is a fixed modelling assumption, and adding it to the search space would grow it past what a twenty-minute budget can usefully explore for a constant this unlikely to be identifiable on its own.
